question: Round 7, crash management for the momentum book (README: 'Round 7 sources'). Momentum is crowded and crash-prone: July 2026 was its worst month on record in several regions. Scaling momentum exposure by the momentum factor's OWN recent volatility roughly doubled its Sharpe ratio and removed most crashes in the papers (Barroso & Santa-Clara 2015; Daniel & Moskowitz 2016). Round 6 scales by SPY's volatility, a proxy; this round scales buys by the volatility of a daily winners-minus-losers portfolio built from the replay's own universe, relative to its one-year median. Tests the level, the factor (WML vs winners alone), a faster estimate, an exposure cap, using it IN PLACE of the SPY filter, the market-volatility version head to head, and on top of cap98_tight.

variants.name: m_rel10
variants.why: scale buys down whenever momentum volatility is above its one-year median

variants.name: m_rel125
variants.why: scale down only when momentum volatility is 25%+ above its median

variants.name: m_rel15
variants.why: scale down only when it is 50%+ above its median (extreme turbulence only)

variants.name: m_abs20
variants.why: the papers' form: a fixed annualised target (20%) instead of a relative one

variants.name: m_win125
variants.why: volatility of the winners leg alone, closer to what a long-only book holds

variants.name: m_fast125
variants.why: a two-month estimate instead of six, to react before a crash is half over

variants.name: m_cap125
variants.why: also no new buys while the invested share is above the scale (closer to scaling the whole book)

variants.name: m_nospy125
variants.why: momentum-volatility scaling INSTEAD of the SPY 2% filter: does continuous scaling replace the on/off switch?

variants.name: r_vol15
variants.why: round 6's market-volatility scaling, repeated head to head

variants.name: ct_base
variants.why: cap98_tight, the tournament challenger, repeated in this run
